documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
26 yo woman, annual.

Doing well overall. Part-time in her MLIS, library job. Palpitations at rest still show up some weeks and not others; sometimes a brief sharp twinge in the chest at rest, seconds long. Never with exertion, no dizziness or fainting. Cardiology follow-up is set for December.

No medications. NKDA. Never smoker; no alcohol.

PE: vitals ok, weight steady. Heart with mid-systolic click and late systolic apical murmur. Lungs clear. Abd benign. Ext no edema.

PHQ-2: 0.

Imp/Plan
#MVP - symptoms stable in character. Keep the December cardiology appointment.
#HCM - flu vaccine given. Updated COVID shot when it is out. Pap due next year.

RTC 12 months.

documents.title: Cardiology Follow-up
documents.author: cardiology
documents.body:
OUTSIDE CARDIOLOGY GROUP - FOLLOW-UP LETTER
Date of visit: 12/22/2023

To the primary care physician,

I saw Abigail today, now 27, for her known mitral valve prolapse. We first evaluated her here in 2021 and saw her again by video in 2022. She continues to get intermittent palpitations and, occasionally, a sharp chest discomfort lasting only moments. Both happen at rest; exercise does not bring them on. No syncope, no dizziness, no recent illness.

She takes no medications. No known drug allergies.
Family history again notable for a mother with MVP and mild MR, a maternal grandmother with a murmur, and a father with hypertension. She does not smoke or use drugs.

Vitals normal.
Heart: 2/6 high-pitched mid-systolic click followed by a late-systolic murmur at the apex. Lungs clear. No JVD, no peripheral edema, no cyanosis.

Assessment: mitral valve prolapse, clinically stable, with recurrent atypical palpitations and chest discomfort.

Plan: continue observation. She knows to come in sooner for fainting or exertional symptoms. Return visit in 1 to 2 years.

Cardiology

documents.body: Cardiology letter from 12/22/23 reviewed. Stable MVP, observation, they will see her in 1-2 years. No change to our plan.

ANNUAL PREVENTIVE EXAM

28 yo F. Still part-time in her library sciences program while working at the university library. Feels well.

MVP: last cardiology visit 12/2023, observation, due back with them sometime this year or next; she hasn't booked it. Palpitations come and go as they always have, at rest, seconds at a time. No fainting, no symptoms with exercise.

Meds: none. NKDA. Never smoker, no alcohol, no drugs.
FHx: mother MVP with mild MR; maternal grandmother murmur; father HTN.

Exam: slender, NAD. Vitals per flowsheet. Neck: no JVD, no thyromegaly. CV: regular, mid-systolic click with late apical systolic murmur. Lungs clear. Abd soft. Ext: no edema. Skin: no concerning lesions.

PHQ-2 0.

Assessment & plan
1. Mitral valve prolapse - clinically unchanged. Encouraged her to schedule the cardiology follow-up.
2. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids today (last labs 2020). Flu vaccine given. COVID at pharmacy if she wants it. Pap current to 2027.

Physical again next September.

documents.body: All of your labs from Tuesday are normal: blood counts, kidney and liver function, sugar, and cholesterol. Nothing to change. Enjoy the fall.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL ED - PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 12/21/2025 15:10

CC: palpitations, lightheaded

HPI: 29 yo female presents with recurrent episodes of her heart fluttering, at rest, today with a few spells of feeling lightheaded while sitting at home. Occasionally a vague discomfort in her chest goes with it. No syncope. States she has had similar palpitations for years and was told she has mitral valve prolapse; outside records not available to us.

Meds: none. Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: mother MVP with mild MR, maternal grandmother with a murmur, father HTN.
Social: no tobacco, no alcohol.

Exam: vitals within normal limits on arrival and at discharge. Thin habitus. Mild scoliosis noted. Heart regular; no murmur appreciated with patient supine. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft. Neuro nonfocal.

ECG: sinus rhythm, no acute changes. CBC and BMP unremarkable.

MDM: young woman with recurrent rest palpitations and lightheadedness, hemodynamically normal, reassuring ECG and labs. Presentation is consistent with mitral valve prolapse as she reports. Recommend outpatient echocardiogram for confirmation, to be arranged with her cardiologist.

Disposition: discharged home in stable condition. Return for fainting, chest pain with exertion, or sustained racing heartbeat. Follow up with cardiology and PCP.

[Received by fax 02/10/2026 in response to records request]

documents.title: ER visit
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, just letting you know I went to the ER on Sunday. The fluttering was happening a lot and I felt lightheaded a couple of times sitting on the couch, which scared me. They did an EKG and bloodwork, said everything looked okay and that it's probably my MVP, and they want me to get an echo through my cardiologist. I'm feeling fine now.

documents.title: RE: ER visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Thanks for telling me, and I'm glad you're feeling better. Please call your cardiology office this week to set up the echo and a follow-up since you're due with them anyway. If you faint, have chest pain with activity, or a racing heartbeat that won't stop, go back to the ER. We'll request the ER record.
